geometry_edits.rationale: Replace the cross-mass with a split-wing organization to create a clearer street-facing void and stronger hierarchy.
Orient the split along the principal long axis so the void can read coherently in plan and elevation.
Keep a legible elevated connection so the mass retains a dominant gesture instead of fragmenting.
Add a ground-spine condition to support the active threshold required by the program.
Shift the roof/section from an arbitrary barrel-like read to a folded section with clearer capacity and daylight consequence.
Keep the section aligned to the long axis so the public void and upper mass remain legible together.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the primary mass from a weak courtyard placeholder into a clearer carved void response to the frontage.
Increase the courtyard cut so the open space becomes legible and usable rather than incidental.
Align the public void with the verified access side.
Lift and clarify the connector so it reads as a public threshold instead of a generic bridge.

rationale: The candidate reads as one central mass with a small attached/crossed upper volume, but the four views do not fully agree on a single coherent dominant gesture. The silhouette is jagged and slightly over-clipped, with the upper element feeling like a stacked protrusion rather than a clear capacity-bearing section. The parcel response is only partial: the mass sits inside the boundary, yet it does not strongly organize the open-space figure along the site edge. Most importantly, the thick blue access edge appears met by a mostly sealed/indirect ground condition; there is no legible public void, court, or undercut that clearly addresses the frontage. Programmatically, neighborhood living wants an active ground threshold and a usable court/terrace sequence, and this form currently reads more like an abstract mass exercise than a plausible compact mixed neighborhood building. The strongest transferable move from the references is a clearer courtyard/bridge public threshold with calmer upper massing and a more intentional street-side void.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More pavilion/community-center than neighborhood-living; copy the void-and-bridge relation, not the cultural roof character.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Strong low-rise civic massing with a central void and an upper bridge/connector that produces a readable public threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Campus-like composition is stronger than the candidate’s single awkward stack; transfer the courtyard hierarchy, not the office typology.
